scenario: Adopt Lintwise as a required pre-merge check (twenty engineers)

motion.text: The team adopts Lintwise, an automated code-quality checker, as a required pre-merge check on the monorepo, subject to the following conditions: (1) a two-week advisory sprint runs first, with all findings reported non-blocking; (2) enforcement blocks merges solely on critical-severity findings—null-derefs, leaked secrets/tokens, dependency CVEs at CVSS 7+, and unparameterized SQL—while all other rules remain advisory; (3) pre-existing issues are suppressed via a baseline snapshot at adoption; (4) Lintwise runs as a parallel CI job with container cache reuse and a sub-ninety-second wall-clock cap; (5) enforcement is gated on Noah's seeded-secret canary passing in two repos and Sana's SQL/config-key canary passing in two pipeline repos; (6) false-positive rate on blocking-tier rules must start at or below 8 percent, published weekly, with any rule exceeding 10 percent for two consecutive weeks auto-demoted to advisory; (7) security-tier findings route exclusively to a separate logged exception path co-owned by Noah and Elena—no self-service waiver by merge authors; (8) a pre-written rollback demotes Lintwise to advisory within 24 hours if p95 queue wait grows by more than ten seconds over baseline during a 20-PR burst or if either canary fails; (9) every blocking finding carries a per-finding "why this matters" message, and a one-page blocking-rules guide is published for new contributors.

objectors.reason: The motion text still reads "adopts … as a required pre-merge check on every repository," which omits the two-week advisory sprint, baseline suppression, severity-tiered blocking, and Theo's "the monorepo" correction we all agreed to; voting on this wording as-is would greenlight immediate enforcement without the safeguards I require to protect test-failure signal from lint noise.

The motion text says "every repository" when we have one monorepo—Theo's fix is still unaddressed—and the bare wording ("required pre-merge check") omits every condition the team agreed is a prerequisite (critical-tier-only blocking, two-week advisory sprint, parallel execution, 24-hour rollback, baseline suppression), so voting on this text would bind us to a policy stricter and vaguer than what we actually endorsed.
The motion still reads "every repository" even though we maintain a single monorepo, so per Theo's fix it must be rewritten to "the monorepo" before a vote, or enforcement scope is ambiguous.

The motion still says "every repository" instead of "the monorepo," and it does not encode the team's agreed advisory-first structure with severity-tiered blocking gated on Noah's secret canary and Sana's SQL canary passing—voting on the bare wording would re-open the two policy reversals I flagged.

chairQuestions.topic: Secret-detection and dependency-CVE rule availability in Lintwise's default install
chairQuestions.experience_sought: Vera ran Lintwise daily for six months on a prior backend-heavy team. On that install, were hardcoded-secret rules (API keys, tokens in config) and dependency-CVE lookup shipped in the default ruleset, or did the team add a separate rule-pack or plug-in? If add-on, what was the configuration effort? If the rules were absent entirely, say so.

chairQuestions.topic: SQL-file first-class parsing and unparameterized-query detection
chairQuestions.experience_sought: Sana stated she read Lintwise documentation. In those docs, are .sql files listed as first-class parse targets with built-in rules for unparameterized WHERE clauses and null-guard drops, or does the parser only match SQL-like string patterns inside Python or JS source? Can you confirm whether noqa-style per-line suppressions are honoured on .sql files specifically?

reminders.quote: I've seen three near-misses this quarter where a key almost shipped in a PR.
Docs confirm container-cached parallel execution, so Mei's ninety-second cap is achievable.

My baseline is 6-minute peak queue wait and 11-minute builds; adding one cached minute in parallel shouldn't extend wall-clock. But I haven't run Lintwise myself—I'm still working from Priya's four-minute default. So I'm for the gate conditional on one thing I own: a 20-PR burst load test during peak queue hours, measuring p95 queue depth and total CI wall-clock. If p95 queue wait stays under 8 minutes and builds under 12, the parallel config is validated and I'll sign off.
crucially, I did *not* tune the ruleset before measuring. That means 30 percent is an untuned floor, not a ceiling—tuned frontend rules should land well under that, but we won't know until the trial.
